sense: belief in God and the worship that goes with it

terms.gloss: religion, reverence for God (the gods), worship
evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.8: religiōne, id est cultū deōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically first of all a feeling: awe and reverence before the divine, and so scruple and conscientiousness, a religious obligation or a taboo; then the observances and the whole system of worship, often in the plural, religiōnēs (Lewis & Short). For the Christian faith see faith.

terms.gloss: the worship of the gods; of God, cultus Deī
terms.grammar: cultus, cultūs m., with a genitive
evidence: Cic. N.D. 1.117: religiōnem, quae deōrum cultū piō continētur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The outward side of religion: worship and its rites.

phrases.latin: religiō est, quae superiōris cujusdam nātūrae (quam dīvīnam vocant) cūram caerimōniamque affert
phrases.english: religion is what brings care for and ceremonies to some higher nature, which men call divine

phrases.latin: Religiōsior tū quidem es, quam prō aetāte. — Immō nūllam aetātem nōn decet religiō.
phrases.english: “You are very devout for your age.” — “But there is no age that devotion does not suit.”
